sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Pamplona regulates on-street parking in colour-coded zones and is tightening access to its old town. The council reported on 27 January 2026 that the city has 34,307 regulated on-street spaces, 18,710 orange and 13,230 blue, and 42,447 active resident and activity permits, with 2,581 resident permits for 686 spaces in the Casco Antiguo [3]. Regulated hours are Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 14:00 and 16:00 to 20:00 and Saturday from 08:30 to 14:00; in the blue zone residents of the sector park without a time limit and others pay, while in the orange zone a ticket is valid for a maximum of one day [4]. On 11 May 2026 the local government board awarded the regulated-parking and tow-truck contract to Dornier for 45.76 million euros over four years, covering the blue zone, all park-and-ride lots, the motorhome lot and access control for the Casco Antiguo and the low-emission zone [5]. The draft ordinance for that zone, approved on 27 August 2025, coincides with the Casco Antiguo controlled-access zone, with penalties planned from 1 May 2026 and about 650 fewer vehicles a day forecast [6]. A press roundup of July 2026 lists Pamplona among the cities already fining 200 euros for entering without a badge, which is the only support we found for sanctions having started [7]. For the San Fermín fiesta of 2026 the council announced that practically the whole city except sector 1 would be an orange zone from 5 to 14 July, and, as a novelty, that the park-and-ride lots would also charge the orange rate [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The developments are about park-and-ride and electric cars. Nine park-and-ride lots with 2,464 spaces, free for 24 hours, recorded 1,463,691 entries in 2024, up 21.8% on 2023, and only 1.53% of entries stayed beyond the free 24 hours [8]. The council counts 3,066 spaces in a dozen park-and-ride lots [3]. It announced on 5 June 2025 that the San Juan lot, with 238 spaces, was ready to open, with licence-plate entry and 24 hours free [9]. In the first two days of paid parking in the twelve lots in July 2026 the council counted 1,117 operations with an average stay of 284 minutes [11]. A proposed four-storey underground car park with 346 spaces in Calle Sangüesa, tendered together with the redevelopment of the Plaza de la Cruz as a 75-year concession, saw works suspended in 2023, and the citizen consultation on it was suspended on 14 December 2023; we found no later status [14][15]. From 1 August 2025 electric cars left in a charging bay more than 15 minutes after charging ends pay 0.20 euro a minute, up to 50 euros; the city then had 29 publicly accessible charging stations with 65 charge points [16]. In September 2024 the council awarded a contract for 51 regulated rotation spaces in front of Pabellón C of the university hospital to ease access to consultations [12].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Eight municipal concession car parks are run by private companies: SABA at Plaza del Castillo, ACVIL at Plaza de Toros, San Roque at Audiencia, Gestión y Aparcamientos Pamplona at Carlos III, a company at Rincón de la Aduana, Empark at Blanca de Navarra and the hospital zone, and a joint venture at the bus station [2]. Their tariffs rose 2.7% on 1 January 2026, with daily maximums of 19.39 euros at Plaza del Castillo, 18.95 at Audiencia, 15.22 at Carlos III, 20.09 at Rincón de la Aduana and 14.01 at Plaza de Toros [0]. The hospital zone has separate rotation tariffs for hospital workers and other users, and monthly tickets cost 13.24 euros for staff and 53.00 euros for others [1]. A council-commissioned audit reported by regional press in February 2023 found all 4,681 resident spaces in the Casco Antiguo and the Ensanche occupied, with 1,001 people on waiting lists, an older figure from a single report whose audit we did not see [13]. The university hospital has 1,290 open-air spaces, 83 of them for disabled users [12].

Our data cover eight car parks, 3,497 spaces together, for 21 days since 30 September 2026. The hospital, with 1,290 spaces, is the fullest, at 79% on weekdays and 90% at weekends, and reached full in a single reading on a Saturday afternoon. Plaza del Castillo (452 spaces) averaged 67% and 70%, Carlos III (291) and Blanca de Navarra (277) about 55% every day, and Plaza de Toros (440) 34% on weekdays and 59% at weekends. The bus-station car park (385) averaged 39% on weekdays and 31% at weekends, and Audiencia (244) only 15% and 14%. Rincón de la Aduana (118) rose from 36% on weekdays to 52% at weekends.
